newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Smoking damages careers, says Brazilian survey.
newsitem.headline: Smoking damages careers, says Brazilian survey.

text.p: Quitting smoking may not only make you healthier, it could help you earn a lot more money, according to a Brazilian survey published on Tuesday.

A survey of 1,325 executives in Brazil's financial centre of Sao Paulo found that smokers earned substantially less than their non-smoking counterparts and that this wage discrepancy increased dramatically with age.

Among executives aged 40-44, smokers earned an average monthly salary of $3,999, or $801 less than non-smokers, according to the survey by consulting firm Case Consultores. Between the ages of 60-64, smokers earned an average of just $2,900 a month, or $2,100 less than non-smokers, the survey found.

"Smokers have less energy, less desire and a character that is resistant to change. This kind of behaviour represents everything businesses don't want," survey coordinator Thomas Case told Jornal do Brasil, which published the results.
Case Consultores polled executives at 30 firms in Sao Paulo. It said 22 percent of those surveyed were smokers, many of whom complained they had missed out on job promotions.
The survey suggested that quitting smoking was the best way to improve a smoker's salary and status within a company, noting 56 percent of non-smoking executives were once smokers.
